title: LServe: Efficient Long-sequence LLM Serving with Unified Sparse Attention
problem: Serving LLMs on long sequences (>64k tokens) is bottlenecked by attention: quadratic complexity during prefill and linear KV cache memory pressure during decode. No existing system addresses both stages simultaneously in a unified framework.
motivation: At 128k tokens, attention accounts for 75%+ of runtime in both prefill and decode stages for Llama-3-8B on A100. KV cache quantization (QServe) reduces memory and bandwidth but does not cut computation count. Dynamic sparse attention (MInference, Quest) reduces compute but does not cut memory and addresses only one stage. A unified system can compound savings multiplicatively.
method: LServe accelerates attention on long sequences by strategically reducing required computations. During prefill, half the attention heads are predetermined to only look at sink tokens (the very beginning) plus recent tokens in a sliding window, while other heads compute normally—both run together in one optimized GPU kernel. During decode, LServe uses a two-level page system: fine-grained logical pages score which key-value memories matter most using query dot products with statistics, while larger physical pages store the actual compressed data; it reuses these scores across consecutive decode steps instead of recalculating them. All key-value data is quantized to 4 bits (W4A8KV4) to minimize memory usage.
key_novelty: LServe's core contribution is unifying static sparse attention heads (predetermined during prefill) with dynamic hierarchical page pruning (during decode) into one fused GPU kernel using quantized key-value storage, speeding up both stages of long-sequence LLM serving.
contributions: Unified block-sparse attention formulation compatible with both static and dynamic sparsity patterns
Hierarchical paging: logical-page importance scoring decoupled from physical-page memory layout to preserve accuracy with large quantized pages
Reusable page selection exploiting temporal locality of attention to cut page selector overhead by 4x
Fused CUDA/PTX kernels integrating streaming head masking, dynamic page lookup, and KV quantization
2.9x prefill speedup and 1.3-2.1x decode speedup over vLLM on Llama-3-8B, Llama-2-7B, Minitron-4B
Demonstrated compatibility with DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B reasoning model at comparable accuracy
hardware_target: NVIDIA A100 80GB GPUs; NVIDIA L40S 48GB GPU; multi-GPU servers
metrics: Time to first token (TTFT, prefill latency)
limitations: Half-head streaming conversion is determined offline and may not optimally adapt to all input distributions
Hierarchical paging adds per-layer kmax/kmin storage overhead (~2x key stats per logical page)
Reusable page selection introduces bounded staleness in KV page selection between chunk boundaries
